newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bond tender provides base for rally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bond tender provides base for rally.

text.p: *Australian bond yields eased back after a A$900 million T-bond tender proved sufficiently well-supported to provide a late rally, but attention is now on supply in the U.S.
*RBA's Macfarlane due to address Sydney Institute later.
Australian bond yields eased back after a A$900 million Treasury bond tender proved sufficiently well supported to produce a late rally, but attention is now on supply in the U.S. later today.

"Bids were a little wider on the 10-year bond than I had expected, but there was wide range of demand for the tender," said one trader. "With the supply absorbed the market is looking in pretty good shape."
The A$600 million of November 2006 stock saw a bid range of three basis points, while the A$300 million of January 2001s fetched bids in a tight one basis point range.
The overall view of the tender was fairly mixed and initially saw the March 10-year bond futures contract hit the day's low on the announcement of the result to 92.550.

Meanwhile, Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane is due to address the Sydney Institute at around 6.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), and the market will be waiting to see if there are any clues on his current thinking on policy.

A Reuters poll of economists taken last Friday gave only a 45 percent chance of another cut in official interest rates following last week's strong wages data, down from 50 percent seen in a survey taken the previous week.

Today's 5.3 percent rise in December housing finance was seen confirming a more buoyant picture for the housing sector during 1997, which is leading some economists to believe that interest rates have now bottomed at 6.0 percent.

Economists at Citibank Australia said the RBA will need to see a stalling in the emerging economic growth and the wages outlook to suggest increases at or below 4.0 percent for another easing to occur.
"It is reasonable to expect the next few RBA Board meetings to conclude with the recommendation of 'monetary policy on hold'," they added.

The local market's rebound saw spreads to the dollar bloc reverse an initial widening against North American bonds, which had taken the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread to 100 basis points at one stage. Only the New Zealand long-end outperformed, recovering from Monday's fall to parity against Australia.
